issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaked into a runtime install_requires, not just CI
issues.detail: The cap is added to core/setup.py under install_requires (or similar runtime deps), which means every downstream user of this package now inherits a setuptools<82 ceiling forever, or at least until someone remembers to rip it out. The mmcv/mmengine breakage is a CI/build-time problem and a wheel-build problem, not a runtime requirement of the core package. Pin it in the CI scripts and the build_pkg helper where it actually matters; do not punish every user's environment because mmcv hasn't shipped a fix. If core/setup.py truly needs it at runtime, the commit message should say why in one line.

issues.description: Three things in one patch: setuptools cap, mmengine source swap, mmdet version bump
issues.detail: This is THREE-PATCHES masquerading as one. (1) cap setuptools<82 for the build, (2) stop installing mmengine from a pinned git SHA and use the PyPI wheel 0.10.7 instead, (3) bump mmdet 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0. Each of these can fail independently and each deserves its own bisect target if CI goes red next week. The mmdet bump in particular is unexplained in the description and is not obviously required by the mmengine/setuptools issue.

issues.description: Duplicate setuptools pin and switch from mim to pip without justification
issues.detail: setup_mmcv.sh pins setuptools<82 again even though build_pkg already does it; if these run in the same env that's redundant, if they don't then the duplication is fine but should be a comment. Also the switch from `mim install mmcv` to `pip install mmcv --no-build-isolation` is a real behavioral change (no-build-isolation means the surrounding env's setuptools is what gets used, which is precisely why the pin matters) and deserves one sentence in the commit message explaining why mim was abandoned. Right now a future maintainer reading this diff has to reverse-engineer the intent from a linked mmcv issue.

issues.description: Empty PR description on a CI-unblocking change
issues.detail: Description is literally blank. For a workaround that pins a major build tool, the commit message and PR body should state: which CI job broke, the error signature, the upstream issue link (good, FIXME comment has it), and the exit criteria for removing the cap. The FIXME comments in-tree are good. The PR body should match.

review.summary: Patch unblocks CI by capping setuptools<82 and swapping the mmengine git pin for a PyPI wheel. The CI-side changes are fine and the FIXME pointers to the upstream mmcv issue are exactly right -- that is how a workaround should be marked. The real problem is that the setuptools<82 cap leaked into core/setup.py's install_requires, which exports a CI workaround as a permanent constraint on every downstream user; that belongs in the build scripts only unless there is a runtime justification nobody wrote down. Secondary: this is three changes in one diff (setuptools cap, mmengine source change, mmdet version bump) and the PR body is empty, which is hostile to the next maintainer who has to bisect this in six months. NEEDS-WORK: pull the setuptools pin out of core/setup.py (or justify it in the commit), and write one paragraph in the PR body explaining the mim->pip switch and the mmdet bump.
